careers.name: Software Developer
careers.description: Build useful products, one line at a time.
roadmap: Python or Java; Git; complexity; arrays and strings
HTML, CSS, JavaScript; accessible interfaces; HTTP
SQL, REST APIs, authentication; testing
Deploy a useful app; document decisions; mock interviews
careers.project: A full-stack placement tracker with login, SQL, tests and a public demo.
careers.interview: Explain the data model, a difficult bug and the tradeoffs in your project.
careers.payWhy: Software can serve many customers at a low marginal cost. Engineers who own reliable, revenue-critical systems can have greater business impact; employer and level explain much of the pay variation.
careers.difficultyWhy: Requires problem solving, debugging unfamiliar systems and keeping software reliable as requirements change. Interviews often add timed coding and design constraints.
careers.advice: Build two well-tested projects and explain your own decisions before collecting more certificates.

progression.work: Fix scoped bugs, write tests and learn code review.
progression.skills: Write correct, readable code and explain tests.
progression.evidence: Consistent work quality, learning and reliable documentation.

progression.work: Own a feature from requirements through deployment and support.
progression.skills: Ship complete features and troubleshoot production issues.
progression.evidence: Independently delivered work, useful feedback and dependable collaboration.

progression.work: Design components, investigate incidents and mentor engineers.
progression.skills: Show sound design decisions and make teammates more effective.
progression.evidence: Broader ownership, measurable improvements and helping others grow.

progression.work: Coordinate technical direction, delivery risks and decisions across a team.
progression.skills: Balance business priorities, system risk and engineering capacity.
progression.evidence: Sound decisions across teams, sustained outcomes and effective mentoring.

careers.name: Data Analyst
careers.description: Turn messy data into clear decisions.
roadmap: Spreadsheets; descriptive statistics; SQL joins and grouping
Python, pandas, missing data and exploratory analysis
Power BI or Tableau; metrics and chart selection
Run a case study; explain decisions and limits
careers.project: An open-data dashboard with reproducible cleaning and three business recommendations.
careers.interview: Practice SQL joins and windows, explain an A/B test and tell a concise data story.
careers.payWhy: Reliable analysis can improve pricing, operations and customer decisions. Strong SQL, domain knowledge and clear business communication increase the usefulness of your work.
careers.difficultyWhy: Messy data, ambiguous metrics, statistical mistakes and stakeholder questions make this more than producing charts.
careers.advice: Start with SQL and one business dataset. Explain three decisions your analysis could change.

progression.work: Clean data, validate spreadsheets and write basic queries.
progression.skills: Build reproducible SQL and verify every metric.
progression.evidence: Consistent work quality, learning and reliable documentation.

progression.work: Own recurring reporting and explain metric changes.
progression.skills: Frame a business question and communicate uncertainty.
progression.evidence: Independently delivered work, useful feedback and dependable collaboration.

progression.work: Design analyses, review data quality and guide junior analysts.
progression.skills: Connect experiments and recommendations to decisions.
progression.evidence: Broader ownership, measurable improvements and helping others grow.

progression.work: Set analytics priorities and help teams use evidence in decisions.
progression.skills: Build reliable analytics processes and coach others.
progression.evidence: Sound decisions across teams, sustained outcomes and effective mentoring.

careers.name: AI / ML Engineer
careers.description: Build models that solve real problems.
roadmap: Python, NumPy, linear algebra, probability and calculus
Supervised learning; baselines; feature engineering
Cross-validation, leakage, class imbalance and error analysis
Serve a model; monitor quality and drift; write tests
careers.project: A reproducible ML service with a baseline, holdout evaluation and inference API.
careers.interview: Explain leakage, precision versus recall and why a simpler baseline may win.
careers.payWhy: Scarce combinations of modelling, software engineering and deployment can be valuable when they improve a real product. Research hype alone does not establish commercial value.
careers.difficultyWhy: Needs mathematics, rigorous evaluation, reproducibility and reliable deployment; weak validation can produce impressive but unusable models.
careers.advice: Master Python, statistics and baselines first. A smaller reproducible project is more persuasive than an unexplained model.

progression.work: Prepare datasets and reproduce a baseline with supervision.
progression.skills: Understand probability, linear algebra and data leakage.
progression.evidence: Consistent work quality, learning and reliable documentation.

progression.work: Train, evaluate and deploy a model against a measurable goal.
progression.skills: Write tested inference services and evaluate holdout results.
progression.evidence: Independently delivered work, useful feedback and dependable collaboration.

progression.work: Own model lifecycle, failure analysis and production quality.
progression.skills: Monitor drift, latency, cost and stakeholder outcomes.
progression.evidence: Broader ownership, measurable improvements and helping others grow.

progression.work: Set technical direction and prioritize ML work against simpler alternatives.
progression.skills: Coach a team and decide when ML is worth using.
progression.evidence: Sound decisions across teams, sustained outcomes and effective mentoring.

careers.name: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.description: Make systems safer by understanding them.
roadmap: TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, Linux and access control
Threat models; secure coding; OWASP fundamentals
Analyze logs; incident triage; detection rules
Practice only in authorized labs; build a defensive portfolio
careers.project: A home-lab incident report showing detection, containment and prevention.
careers.interview: Walk through an alert investigation and separate evidence from assumptions.
careers.payWhy: Security work can reduce disruption, fraud and regulatory exposure. Pay can grow with scarce defensive expertise and responsibility for critical systems.
careers.difficultyWhy: Requires systems knowledge, continuous learning and careful judgement under uncertainty; realistic incidents are not tidy textbook questions.
careers.advice: Use authorized labs and defensive projects. Never test systems without permission.

progression.work: Triage alerts and document evidence under supervision.
progression.skills: Learn networking, Linux and careful documentation.
progression.evidence: Consistent work quality, learning and reliable documentation.

progression.work: Investigate incidents and improve detection rules.
progression.skills: Distinguish a real incident from noise and explain evidence.
progression.evidence: Independently delivered work, useful feedback and dependable collaboration.

progression.work: Engineer controls, threat models and response processes.
progression.skills: Build effective defenses and validate their coverage.
progression.evidence: Broader ownership, measurable improvements and helping others grow.

progression.work: Prioritize security risks and coordinate cross-team response.
progression.skills: Communicate risk, lead incident response and mentor analysts.
progression.evidence: Sound decisions across teams, sustained outcomes and effective mentoring.

Compute, storage, IAM, DNS and cost controls
Docker, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code
Monitoring, incident review, scaling and recovery

careers.interview: Troubleshoot a failed deployment and explain reliability and cost tradeoffs.
careers.payWhy: Availability, release speed and infrastructure cost affect the whole business. Engineers who improve reliability and operate large platforms may have wider scope.

exams.detail: Some vacancies use GATE; others run a separate test and interview. A GATE score does not guarantee shortlisting or a job.
exams.syllabus: Technical subject test or accepted GATE score, followed by notified selection stages.
after: Check one specific PSU / ISRO / DRDO vacancy and accepted degree
Complete its test, shortlisting, interview and document requirements
Join only after appointment and required checks
Progress according to that organisation’s technical and promotion framework
exams.advice: There is no single PSU exam, cutoff, pay scale or promotion policy. ISRO and DRDO also have distinct recruitment rules.
difficultyReasons: Different organisations use different selection routes
exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Check one specific PSU / ISRO / DRDO vacancy and accepted degree.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

roleExample.label: ISRO scientist / engineer example

stages.work: Contribute to assigned engineering or scientific design, implementation and testing.
Own more complex technical work and demonstrate independent problem solving.
Take broader subsystem, research or technical review responsibility.
Provide greater technical leadership and coordinate complex work.

roleExample.skills: Develop deep domain knowledge, rigorous verification, technical documentation, independent judgement and mentoring. ISRO’s assessment scheme and official requirements control progression. This is not a universal PSU or DRDO ladder.

exams.name: CMAT / XAT / NMAT
exams.eligibility: Graduation or the final-year routes allowed by each exam; institute-level conditions vary.
exams.detail: These are separate examinations. Check each official bulletin, marks requirements and accepted colleges independently.
exams.syllabus: Quantitative skills, language, reasoning and exam-specific sections.
exams.verified: Separate official rules for each exam
after: Apply separately to programmes that accept the selected exam
Meet interview and institution-specific admission stages
Complete the management programme and build functional skills
Explore recruitment into finance, marketing, operations, analytics and other roles
exams.advice: CMAT, XAT and NMAT are separate examinations. Their scores, scales and cutoffs cannot be treated as interchangeable.
difficultyReasons: Different scoring scales and exam-specific sections
exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Apply separately to programmes that accept the selected exam.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

exams.name: UGC NET / CSIR NET
exams.eligibility: Often a qualifying postgraduate degree. Some four-year UG routes exist with restricted purposes and marks requirements.
exams.detail: Do not assume a three-year bachelor’s alone is sufficient. JRF age, category relaxation and PhD / teaching eligibility differ.
exams.syllabus: Subject knowledge plus the applicable general / research aptitude components.
exams.verified: Usually a later-stage pathway • check bulletin
after: Use the result only for the category of qualification stated on the certificate
Apply for eligible PhD / JRF / Assistant Professor routes as applicable
Meet separate fellowship, admission or recruitment conditions
Academic progression depends on appointment, qualifications and institutional rules
exams.advice: JRF, Assistant Professor eligibility and PhD admission categories differ. A four-year UG route does not automatically establish teaching eligibility.
difficultyReasons: Different qualification categories and separate admission rules
exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Use the result only for the category of qualification stated on the certificate.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

exams.name: ICAI CA examinations
exams.eligibility: Foundation and direct-entry routes follow different education and marks requirements.
exams.detail: Confirm the current ICAI scheme, registration, training and examination rules. A commerce degree does not itself confer the CA qualification.
exams.syllabus: Foundation / Intermediate / Final as applicable, plus required practical training.
after: Complete the applicable ICAI examination stages
Complete practical training and other scheme requirements
Apply for membership and authorised professional routes as required
Specialise in audit, tax, financial reporting, corporate finance or practice
exams.advice: Passing one group is progress, not completion of the CA qualification. Use the current ICAI scheme.
exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Complete the applicable ICAI examination stages.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

exams.name: AIBE / Postgraduate Law
exams.eligibility: AIBE and postgraduate law entrances have different qualifying-degree and registration rules.
exams.detail: Use the current AIBE rules for practice-related requirements; check each university’s LLM entrance separately.
exams.syllabus: Legal subjects and the current official exam pattern.
after: Satisfy current Bar Council, enrolment and AIBE requirements
Obtain the applicable certification for practice
Build a specialisation through supervised legal experience
Progress in a firm, chamber, in-house team or independent practice
exams.advice: AIBE is a professional qualifying route. LLM admissions are separate and have different selection rules.
difficultyReasons: Preparation must follow the current permitted-material rules
exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Satisfy current Bar Council, enrolment and AIBE requirements.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

exams.name: NEET PG / INI-CET
exams.eligibility: The relevant medical qualification, registration and internship completion rules must be met by the announced cutoff.
exams.detail: NEET PG and INI-CET use separate official notices. Verify current NBEMS, AIIMS and NMC requirements for your route.
exams.syllabus: Medical subjects and clinical reasoning in the notified test format.
after: Meet the qualifying result and current counselling conditions
Seek a PG seat through the applicable counselling route
Complete approved supervised postgraduate training
Develop specialist practice, research or teaching within registration rules
exams.advice: NEET PG and INI-CET are separate. Qualifying percentiles can be revised; a qualifying mark does not assure a preferred specialty or seat.
difficultyReasons: Category, specialty, institute and round-specific seat competition
exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Meet the qualifying result and current counselling conditions.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

exams.name: GPAT
exams.eligibility: An eligible B.Pharm / permitted final-year route under the current official GPAT bulletin.

exams.syllabus: Pharmaceutical sciences and the notified official syllabus.

Complete admission and any separate funding requirements
Develop a subject specialisation and supervised research
Explore quality, research, regulatory or later academic roles

exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Apply to eligible M.Pharm and related accepted programmes.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

exams.name: GRE / GMAT / English tests
exams.eligibility: Test registration and admission eligibility are separate; the target university decides accepted scores and qualifications.
exams.detail: Degree, score validity, English-test waivers, costs and visa requirements vary. Check each target programme.
exams.syllabus: GRE / GMAT reasoning; IELTS / TOEFL English skills as applicable.
after: Select universities and programmes that actually accept the test
Meet degree, language, funding and application conditions
Complete the selected programme and build relevant work skills
Explore eligible jobs or research subject to local employment and immigration rules
exams.advice: GRE, GMAT and language tests use different scales. They do not have one universal pass mark or guarantee admission, funding or employment.

exams.whyChoose: Consider this route when its subject and destination match your goal: Select universities and programmes that actually accept the test.
exams.payWhy: The resulting institution, qualification, employer and role affect pay. The exam score itself is not a salary entitlement.

competitions.name: ICPC
competitions.description: University team programming contest: form a team of three from one institution and work with a coach.
competitions.eligibility: Enrollment, period-of-eligibility, previous participation and regional rules apply. Your coach should confirm the current 2026/27 rules; a branch match alone is not proof.
competitions.prep: C++ / Java / Python, data structures, graphs, dynamic programming and regular five-hour team practice.

competitions.name: Smart India Hackathon
competitions.description: Solve problem statements through the institution’s published SIH selection process.
competitions.eligibility: Check the current SIH guidelines, institutional nomination, team composition and problem-statement conditions.
competitions.prep: Understand one problem deeply, validate with users, build a working prototype and rehearse a clear demo.

competitions.name: Kaggle competitions
competitions.description: Practice applied machine learning on competition datasets.
competitions.eligibility: Age, location, team size, licences and prize eligibility depend on each competition’s rules.
competitions.prep: Start with a baseline, prevent leakage, use appropriate validation and document experiments.

competitions.name: Google Summer of Code
competitions.description: Contribute to an open-source organisation through a mentored project. This is a programme, not an entrance exam.
competitions.eligibility: Check the current contributor age, residency, prior participation and open-source experience rules.
competitions.prep: Read contribution guides, reproduce an issue, make small contributions and discuss a realistic proposal.

competitions.name: Codeforces & AtCoder
competitions.description: Regular online contests to improve algorithmic reasoning.
competitions.eligibility: Read contest-specific conditions; rated division, age and prize rules can vary.
competitions.prep: Practice fundamentals, compete at your level, then upsolve missed problems and record mistakes.
